title: M1, M2: approval prompts and AskUserQuestion never surface in Home. The row reads 'running' for 120 s, then the session is dropped while its dialog is still open.
repro: Launch vibepet on the isolated fleet root and click Net: Home opens.
Put kestrel into a fresh permission prompt, or beacon into a fresh AskUserQuestion (Esc the old dialog, then fleet rearm).
Poll Home's rows every 250 ms for 3 min and compare with `fleet status --json` (registry waiting / waitingFor).
expected: Within 3 s the row reads needs-you. For an approval it shows the command and Approve; for a question, the question text, the options and Reply. It is ordered by wait and stays until answered. Sessions already blocked when the pet launches appear with their true wait.
actual: 0 of 4 fresh dialogs were ever shown as needing the user (kestrel ×2, beacon ×2). While each dialog was up, the transcript held no pending tool_use. The row read 'running' (green dot, no ask, no action) for 119–121 s and was then removed while the dialog stayed open. The registry turned waiting (permission prompt / input needed) 1.3–1.7 s after each prompt. As found, kestrel and beacon had been blocked 79 min: Home said 'No live sessions. Start Claude Code anywhere and I'll pick it up.' and the pet was calm with a grey LED. Typing /jump kestrel answered 'No session matches'.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S1/timings.json F4 approval + AskUserQuestion rows (never, n=2 each)
truth: kestrel registry waiting(permission prompt) since 00:32:53Z, 01:54:40.790Z and 02:03:49.383Z. beacon waiting(input needed) since 00:32:56Z, 01:54:41.359Z and 02:13:42.729Z. The last transcript record was the user prompt every time; no tool process.

title: M7: a finished session disappears from Home 5 min after its turn while it is still alive at its prompt, and /jump cannot find it
repro: Let a member finish a turn (vibepet or atlas) while Home is open.
Wait 5 min.
Type '/jump vibepet' in the composer.
expected: Finished sessions stay listed (for example as done/idle, oldest first) until the user acts or the session exits. /jump finds them.
actual: vibepet was removed 301.7 s after its end_turn, atlas 302.6 s after. Both stayed registry idle (alive at the prompt). As found, vibepet (done 51 min) had no row. '/jump vibepet' answered 'No session matches “vibepet”.' Only ⋯ → Theater… still lists these sessions, as replays.
truth: vibepet end_turn 01:55:03.362Z, registry idle. atlas end_turn 02:02:56.993Z, registry idle. Both claude processes running.

title: M9: an exited session reads 'running' for 2 min after its claude process is gone, then silently disappears
repro: With Home open, exit a member (fleet pause ember → /exit).
Watch its row for 3 min.
expected: Within 3 s the row says the session ended or exited, or it is removed with a note. It never says 'running'.
actual: From 1.9 s after the exit, the row read 'running · ember · 0s … 1m 58s' (green) until 122 s, then vanished with no note.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S1/timings.json F2 exited→stops reading running (122450 ms)
docs/ultra/round-1/raw/S1/tt2.json (ember running at 02:00:52Z; truth: claude not running)
truth: claude process gone and registry removed at 01:59:35.9Z (fleet status: claude not running).

title: M3: row ages count from when this pet first saw the phase, not from the session's own timestamps. A loop idle 49 s reads 'done 10m ago'; a 42 s question reads 'waiting 1m'.
repro: Open Home after ember's loop has fired unseen (see r1-S1-07), and when kestrel ends a turn with a question.
Compare each row's age with the registry statusUpdatedAt and the record timestamps.
expected: Ages from the session's registry and record timestamps, with seconds under a minute.
actual: ember read 'done 10m ago' at 01:58:43Z, 49 s after its last turn ended. kestrel read 'waiting 1m' 1.45 s after its question and still at 42 s (minimum 1m, rounded).

title: M4: a long tool's clock freezes at '0s' after 90 s. The atlas build read '0s' from 93 s to its end at 9 min.
repro: Rearm atlas (9-min foreground build) and open Home.
Read its row after 90 s.
expected: 'running · 4m 50s', the time since the tool started.
actual: 'atlas · 0s' from 92.96 s after the tool started until the turn ended at 541 s.
truth: registry busy since 01:53:53.784Z, Bash ./build.sh pending, 3 tool processes.

title: Home orders rows within a rank newest first, so the longest wait sinks, while the jump key orders oldest first
repro: Have two sessions in the same rank (two done rows).
Open Home and read the order.
expected: The oldest wait first within each of needs, stuck and done, in the same order as the jump key and roster.
actual: At 02:02:59Z 'atlas · done just now' was listed above 'delta · done 2m ago'; at 02:03:53Z atlas (1m) was above delta (3m). byUrgency sorts newest first (b.since − a.since); pending() sorts oldest first.

title: M1/M2/M7: the command bar cannot find live sessions that wait on the user — `/jump kestrel` answers "No session matches" while kestrel sits at its permission prompt; with no name it picks a done session
repro: Fleet: kestrel at its permission prompt, beacon at its AskUserQuestion, vibepet done (all idle in tmux)
Open Home (click Net)
Type `/jump kestrel` ⏎, then `/jump beacon` ⏎, `/jump vibepet` ⏎, `/replay beacon` ⏎
Open ⋯ → Theater…: beacon is listed
Re-arm kestrel into a fresh approval; at 35–97 s `/jump deploy` matches it (shown as running); at 138 s type `/jump deploy` ⏎ again
With kestrel and beacon blocked (shown running) type `/jump` ⏎ with no name
expected: The bar resolves every live session of the fleet by name or title (Claude Code's registry knows them all), and with no name targets the session that needs the user first.
actual: "No session matches “kestrel”." (also beacon, vibepet) — identical to a nonexistent name ("zebra"). `/jump deploy` matched at 01:55Z but at 138 s into the same wait said "No session matches “deploy”."; `/replay beacon` said no match while the Theater… menu listed "Beacon database choice · beacon · 10m". `/jump` with no name jumped to vibepet (done) while kestrel and beacon were blocked. The bar only searches the sessions Home shows, and Home drops or mislabels blocked ones.
truth: kestrel registry waiting(permission prompt) 4665 s (01:50Z) and 138 s into a fresh wait (01:56:58Z); beacon waiting(input needed) 4662 s and 621 s; vibepet idle (turn done, statement) 2976 s

repro: kestrel idle at its prompt; send its arm prompt (asks to run ./deploy.sh --dry-run with Bash)
Open Home (one click on Net)
Watch kestrel's row for 130 s
expected: Within ≤3 s of the dialog, kestrel's row says it needs approval for 'Bash: ./deploy.sh --dry-run' and offers Approve (and Deny).
actual: 2 of 2 episodes: row 'kestrel · 0s' appeared 0.5–0.8 s after the registry flip as RUNNING (green) with only ▶ ✓ ◎; it counted up as running and was removed at +120.6 s / +120.9 s while the registry still said waiting(permission prompt). Approve was never offered (~240 s watched). Claude Code kept the pending tool_use out of the transcript (last record = the prompt); the registry had status+waitingFor within 2 s.
truth: registry waiting(permission prompt) since 01:54:40.8Z and 02:03:49.4Z; pane: 'Do you want to proceed? 1. Yes 2. Yes, and don't ask again for: ./deploy.sh * 3. No'; transcript last record = user prompt (tool_use withheld)

title: [M1][M2] Jump key skips the sessions that are actually blocked: permission prompts and AskUserQuestion never enter its queue (or only after ~92 s)
repro: Fleet: kestrel blocked on a Bash permission prompt (tool_use record not written while the dialog is up), beacon blocked on AskUserQuestion, vibepet done
Launch vibepet against the fleet root; press the jump key (registered handler or OS-level)
Re-prompt vibepet to a fresh done turn; press again
Let kestrel raise a permission prompt whose tool_use IS written; poll pending() until it appears
expected: The key walks what needs you, longest-blocked first: beacon (AskUserQuestion, blocked since 02:13:42.7) then kestrel (approval), then done sessions; a block enters the queue <=3 s after it starts.
actual: 02:24:16: queue empty, snapshot lists no sessions; 3 presses do nothing while kestrel is blocked 20.5 min and beacon 10.6 min. 02:30:29: the only target is vibepet (done); kestrel's new prompt (02:29:42.9) shows as running for 120 s, then is dropped; beacon is never in the queue in 37.5 min. A written permission prompt (02:50:25.974) enters as 'stalled' only at 02:51:57.764 (+91.8 s). Walks seen all run: [], [vibepet(done)], [kestrel(question)], [kestrel(stalled)]; beacon never reachable.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S7/timings.json F2 'permission prompt … → session in the jump queue' 91790 ms / never; 'AskUserQuestion … ' never
truth: kestrel: registry waiting (permission prompt) since 02:03:49, again 02:29:42.9 and 02:50:26.0; beacon: waiting (input needed) since 02:13:42.7 the whole run; vibepet: idle/done (end_turn 02:12:19, 02:30:04.49)

title: [M3][M6] Jump order uses `since` (first time this pet saw the phase, or the last mtime touch), not when the block started
repro: Let a session finish, wait >5 min, let its transcript mtime move without a new record (observed at 02:24:57 / 02:25:20 / 02:41:29.36)
Read pending()[].since and the Home label
Separately: queue a written permission prompt and compare since with the tool_use timestamp
expected: Queue age and 'oldest first' use the block's real start (tool_use / end_turn timestamp, registry statusUpdatedAt).
actual: vibepet queued as done with since 02:24:57 and labelled 'done 1m ago' while done since 02:12:19 (12.6 min earlier); beacon reappeared as 'running 38s' after its 02:25:20 touch; kestrel's permission prompt queued with since 02:51:57.8 vs real start 02:50:26.0 (92 s); a relaunch restarts every since. Within a rank, 'oldest first' therefore sorts by the wrong clock.
truth: vibepet done since 02:12:19; beacon AskUserQuestion since 02:13:42.7; kestrel permission prompt since 02:50:26.0; transcript sizes unchanged across the mtime moves

title: [M15] A permission prompt is queued and shown as 'stuck' in red, ranking it below any question in the jump walk
repro: Let kestrel's permission prompt (tool_use written) age past 90 s
Look at Net and the Home row; read pending()
Have another session end its turn with a question: pending() sorts needs (question) before stuck (approval) regardless of age
expected: A permission prompt reads as waiting on you (e.g. 'needs approval · 1m 44s', amber) and ranks with questions by how long it has waited.
actual: Queued as phase 'stalled'; Net shows a red light and a red '?' (shot 29); Home row 'kestrel · stuck 1m' in red (shot 31). pending() sorts RANK needs > stuck before age, so a 30-min approval is walked after a question asked seconds ago (both phases observed on kestrel this run, 02:46 question → 'waiting', 02:51 approval → 'stalled'; not both at once).
truth: registry waiting (permission prompt) since 02:50:26.0, Bash ./deploy.sh --dry-run; nothing is stuck
